summary: ORCHESTRATOR-ADJUDICATED (unhappy-path flagged for possible escalation to HIGH pending confirmation whether delete+recreate-same-rule_id is a supported workflow; I independently investigated rather than relaying the uncertainty). Read guaranteed_state_store.cpp end to end (confirmed UNCHANGED by this diff - 0-line diff on the file) and guardian_routes.cpp's rollup_by_rule/render_status_fragment (the pre-existing dashboard analog). FINDING: this diff's catalogue-intersection defense (added in 1e99abb10) correctly excludes an orphan census row for a rule_id that STAYS deleted, but does NOT and cannot protect against rule_id REUSE - once a new rule exists under the reused rule_id, rule_names() includes it again and a stale census row from the OLD rule's lifecycle is silently re-admitted and misattributed to the NEW rule. Verified this is NOT a new exposure this diff introduces: guardian_routes.cpp's pre-existing rollup_by_rule has the IDENTICAL blind spot via the same underlying tables (by_rule keyed by rule_id, looked up against the live rules catalogue, with no rule-generation/created_at cross-check) - so provenance is PRE-EXISTING, a store/schema-design gap (no rule 'generation' token distinguishing a rule_id's successive lifetimes), not introduced or worsened by this diff. What IS new: this diff is the first place that turns the underlying signal into a bare, single, authoritative-looking INTEGER (errored_rules) that a SIEM/automation client might poll and act on without the dashboard's contextual cues (creation timestamp, 'no device reports yet' framing) that make a human more likely to notice something looks wrong. EXPOSURE E5 (requires BOTH ordinary propagation lag AND a deliberate, unusual choice to reuse the exact same rule_id rather than a fresh one on recreation - no evidence found that delete+recreate-same-ID is an encouraged or common authoring workflow; this is a genuinely rare compound sequence, not the ordinary case). Recommend: product confirm whether delete+recreate-same-rule_id is a supported workflow; if so, close the gap at create_rule (pre-emptively delete any lingering guardian_agent_rule_status rows for rule_id before the INSERT closes the window regardless of arrival timing) rather than only at the two new REST reads.

trigger: the per-agent route's SECOND store read (rule_names_for) fails AFTER the FIRST read (agent_rule_statuses_for_agent) already succeeded and was audited as success
summary: CORRECTION to my own prior ledger annotation (mis-transcribed by workflow-orchestrator when recording this row, not a sub-agent error): this row is NOT the same finding as CONS-2, and the earlier 'matches CONS-2's finding' note was wrong. Re-read the handler directly to resolve Gate 6b's flagged disagreement. The single emit_behavioral_audit call fires once, right after the FIRST read, recording statuses_result?"success":"failure" BEFORE the early-return check on that same result. A SECOND read (rule_names_for) can still fail afterward, producing a 503 with NO further audit call - so when read-1 succeeds and read-2 fails, the audit row says 'success' while the caller actually received a 503. This matches the codebase's documented 'over-audit, never under-audit' posture (the same posture CONS-2 itself cites from dex_routes.cpp) - defensible, not a bug, correctly NICE. CONS-2 is a DIFFERENT, DISTINCT finding: it's about what happens when the FIRST read itself fails (this route audits it as 'failure', a real audit row) vs device-compliance's analogous pre-lookup fault (baseline_store_ok, which produces NO audit row at all) - a genuine 'same shape' comment inaccuracy, correctly SHOULD. Both findings stand independently; this is a band-neutral correction of a mis-recorded relationship (UP-4 stays NICE, CONS-2 stays SHOULD, neither's severity or gate status changes), so no adjudicated_by is required per the de-escalation rule.
